findings.excerpt: nsmulPt ER.L t n Q = ER.L.nsmul t n Q
findings.problem: The library has two parallel definitions of the n-fold multiple of a point. `RelativeGroupLaw.nsmul` has simp lemmas `nsmul_zero` and `nsmul_succ` and the lemma `nsmul_natural`. `nsmulPt` is a separate structurally recursive definition with no simp lemmas and no bridge lemma. As a result, simp has no normal form for `nsmulPt`. This proof has to prove the bridge by induction and unfold it with `show`, then re-enter it with `rw [hΨP, nsmulPt_eq, ← ER.L.nsmul_natural, ← nsmulPt_eq, ...]`. That rewrites in both directions and picks an ad hoc normal form.
findings.proposed_change: In Def_CerednikDrinfeld_QMModuli, next to `nsmulPt`, add `@[simp] theorem nsmulPt_zero` and `@[simp] theorem nsmulPt_succ`, which are `rfl` equations in the same shape as `nsmul_zero` and `nsmul_succ`. Also add `theorem nsmulPt_eq_nsmul (L) (t) (n) (P) : nsmulPt L t n P = L.nsmul t n P`. Make it `@[simp]` only if `nsmul` is chosen as the canonical form. Otherwise orient it the other way and add `nsmulPt_natural`. Then this local `have` can be dropped, and the `Ψ_nsmul` step and the `hP'tor` rewrite chain can use the shared lemmas.
findings.benefit: Every file that reasons about `nsmulPt` (the QM level and torsion theorems) would normalize to one form and could reuse `nsmul_natural`. The torsion proofs would no longer re-prove the bridge by hand with `show`.
